A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SpikeLLM, GIF neurons and Optimal Brain Spiking for 7–70B-parameter language models. All 15 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable. Methods, equations, experiments and displays can be matched across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantization experiments, perplexity and zero-shot accuracy results, saliency ablations, calibration-data sensitivity, and structured-versus-unstructured comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains original SpikeLLM experiments and adds results involving QuaRot, QLoRA and EfficientQAT, alongside operation-count analysis.

M1.justification: The core GIF/OBSpiking framework and ternary variant remain. However, the specified neuron rules change: v2 Eq. 1 subtracts the token minimum and resets using the preceding spike, while v2 Eq. 7 specifies a per-token threshold instead of the separate per-channel thresholds accompanying v1 Eq. 9. These are limited revisions to the reported quantizer formulation.

E1.justification: The WikiText2/C4 and six commonsense benchmarks remain. Appendix A.5.2 adds Alpaca fine-tuning and evaluation across humanities, STEM, social and other subject groups, extending coverage beyond the earlier calibration and commonsense evaluations. Table 11 does not explicitly name the subject-wise evaluation benchmark.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated comparisons with QuaRot-RTN/GPTQ in Table 4; NormalFloat, QLoRA variants, QA-LoRA and IR-QLoRA in Table 11; and GPTQ, AutoRound, AQLM and EfficientQAT in Table 12. The original main-table comparators and PB-LLM comparisons remain. OmniQ in Table 12 corresponds to the existing OmniQuant baseline.

E3.justification: New protocols include QuaRot-based RTN/GPTQ comparisons with 20–30% salient channels, Alpaca QLoRA fine-tuning, and two-stage EfficientQAT training at sequence length 2048. v2 introduces Sparse ACE for binary inference. The calibration-data sensitivity experiment now specifies loss augmentation, whereas v1's stated 7B configuration disabled it. These changes extend the experimental design substantially.

E4.justification: Table 5 adds an operation-count analysis comparing multi-bit GEMM and expanded binary inference. The calibration-data sensitivity study is revised. Existing matched-cost, random-channel, activation/KV-cache and structured-versus-unstructured analyses remain; their relocation and figure rearrangement do not constitute new ablations.

E5.justification: The reported calibration-sampling study changes from 40 training repetitions in v1 Appendix A to 16 in v2 Appendix A.2.2, with a revised scatter plot. Both retain paired seeds between methods and seed 2 elsewhere. Neither adds confidence intervals or significance tests; this is a revision to the reported repetition count.

E6.justification: The main zero-shot table is extensively revised; v2 also explicitly labels several metrics as normalized, so score changes cannot automatically be treated as same-setting gains. Perplexities change too: LLAMA-2-7B W4A4 SpikeLLM T=2 WikiText2 PPL changes from 11.36 to 11.93. Table 10 drops the former W2A8 T=2 and W2A16 T=4 rows. New comparison and operation results are added, while the PB-LLM table and structured/unstructured scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The main saliency theorem and proof are largely retained, but the Hessian definition changes from H=XX^T to H=2XX^T. The neuron equations are revised, Appendix A.4.2 adds explicit firing-rate and terminal-potential conditions with an IF/binary-GIF equivalence argument, and Sparse ACE is newly defined. These are limited formal additions and corrections.

C1.justification: The first 7–70B spiking-LLM, saliency-based quantization and additive-linear-layer claims remain. v2 elevates explicit spike-length compression and dual GEMM/event-driven implementation into headline contributions and strengthens the framing from offering an alternative to claiming that comparisons prove the necessity of spiking. The abstract also switches its highlighted result from LLAMA-2-7B to LLAMA-7B.

C2.justification: v2 adds specific interpretations: saliency remains useful after rotation, multi-bit GIF training reduces accumulated quantization error, and binary expansion trades additional operations for asynchronous inference. A new limitations paragraph acknowledges the performance gap to ANN LLMs and suggests continued pretraining. The earlier structured/unstructured deployment tradeoff remains.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code release; v2 states that code is public and supplies a repository address. v2 additionally reports approximately 3.5 hours on one A100-80 GPU for a 7B model, GPTQ block size 128, evaluator versions and normalized metric labels, and detailed training/inference explanations in Appendix A.4. These substantially improve documented reproducibility, although repository availability was not independently checked.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and discussion concerning QuaRot, EfficientQAT, QLoRA, IR-QLoRA, SNN-BERT and additional quantization/mobile-model work. It explains compatibility with rotation and fine-tuning approaches while retaining the central positioning relative to OBS, SNNs and conventional quantization. The SparseGPT and MiniLLM references from v1 are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and contribution narrative are substantially rewritten. Low-bit quantization moves from Section 3.1 to Appendix A.1, saliency-aware spiking receives a separate subsection, experimental discussion is reorganized, and conclusion, limitations and expanded appendix subsections are added. Citation style, author information and conference headers also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds an encoding overview, firing-function and training/inference diagrams, plus encoding, configuration, efficiency and new comparison tables. Existing figures are redrawn or rearranged, including reordered ablation panels and a changed horizontal-axis representation. The perplexity table moves to Appendix A.5.1. These substantially change the visual presentation beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: Broader comparisons, clearer GIF training/inference explanations and added reproducibility information improve the paper's support and usability. New reporting inconsistencies temper those gains: the abstract's 11.01% PPL reduction disagrees with Table 1's 11.85-to-9.98 values, and Table 4's LLAMA-2-13B FP16 average is 80.69 although its six scores average about 73.20. The net improvement is useful but limited.
